_comment: Diagnostic surface for the verify step. This project is a Discord bot, and
it is a SINGLETON: one Discord token, one data/state.json, one data/bot.pid.
Starting a second instance from a build worktree would fight the live bot
for the gateway connection and corrupt shared state.
So verification here does NOT boot its own copy. It drives the bot that is
already running (scripts/discord_test.py talks to it over real webhooks and
reads back what it actually rendered), checks health from the log, and runs
the standalone harnesses for pure display/parse logic.
Only use 'start'/'stop' if the log check reports the bot is DOWN.

_note: send/read go through TEST_WEBHOOK_URL / TEST_LOBBY_WEBHOOK_URL and are
treated as user messages (TEST_WEBHOOK_IDS bypasses the bot-author guard),
so this is a genuine end-to-end action -> observe loop against the live bot.
'read' returns message content, embeds and buttons — which is how you check
what a result message actually RENDERED, not just that it was sent.

harnesses._note: Standalone runners for logic with no live surface. Exit 0 = pass.

auth._note: No HTTP admin surface. Credentials live in .env (DISCORD_TOKEN, TEST_WEBHOOK_URL, TEST_LOBBY_WEBHOOK_URL, TEST_WEBHOOK_IDS) and are read by the scripts above — never pass them on the command line.
